_help: Each paragraph is a list of segments. A plain string is read by the narrator and split into sentences automatically. A one-key object like {"Pip": "text"} is dialogue read with that character's voice. After editing, run: .venv/bin/python tools/generate_audio.py

summary.es: Un zorrito encuentra una estrella que se cayó del cielo y promete ayudarla a volver a casa.
summary.en: A little fox finds a star that fell from the sky and promises to help her get back home.

chapters.title: The Star in the Meadow
paragraphs: Once upon a time, at the edge of a quiet forest, there lived a little fox named Pip. Pip had a fluffy orange tail and a nose that loved to sniff out adventures.
One night, Pip could not sleep. He peeked out of his den and saw something strange. A tiny light was falling from the sky! It tumbled down, down, down, and landed softly in the meadow.
Pip tiptoed through the tall grass. There, between two daisies, was a little star. She was glowing, but only a tiny bit. And she was crying.
whispered Pip.
sniffled the star.

paragraphs.Twinkle: “My name is Twinkle. I was playing tag with the moon, and I slipped. Now I can't get home.”

paragraphs: Pip looked up. The sky was very, very far away. But Pip had a kind heart, and kind hearts always find a way.
said Pip.

paragraphs.Pip: “I will help you get home. I promise.”

paragraphs: Twinkle stopped crying. Her light grew just a little bit brighter. And together, the fox and the star began to make a plan.

chapters.title: The Tallest Hill

paragraphs.Twinkle: “Where is the closest place to the sky?”

paragraphs: asked Twinkle.
Pip thought and thought. Then his ears popped up.

paragraphs.Pip: “Grandpa Owl will know! He knows everything.”

paragraphs: So Pip carried Twinkle carefully in his paws, and they walked to the oldest tree in the forest. Grandpa Owl was sitting on a branch, blinking his big yellow eyes.

paragraphs.Owl: “Hoo, hoo. What do we have here?”

paragraphs: said Grandpa Owl.
said Pip.

paragraphs.Pip: “She fell from the sky. We need to find the closest place to the stars.”

paragraphs: Grandpa Owl smiled.

paragraphs.Owl: “Climb the Tallest Hill, beyond the river. At the very top, the sky is close enough to touch. But hurry! Twinkle must be home before the sun wakes up.”

paragraphs: Pip and Twinkle set off. They crossed the river by hopping on stones. One, two, three! They climbed over rocks and through prickly bushes. Pip's legs grew tired, but he did not stop.
said Twinkle softly.
Pip smiled.
he said. And step by step, they climbed higher and higher.

chapters.title: Home in the Sky
paragraphs: At last, Pip reached the top of the Tallest Hill. The wind was cool, and the stars looked so close that Pip could almost count their sparkles.
cheered Pip.
But Twinkle was worried.

paragraphs.Twinkle: “I'm still too small and too dim to fly,”

paragraphs: she said.

paragraphs.Twinkle: “How will I get back up there?”

paragraphs: Pip had an idea.

paragraphs.Pip: “Maybe you need to feel happy to shine bright. Let's think of happy things!”

paragraphs: So they did. They thought about warm sunshine, and lazy rivers, and the funny way Grandpa Owl said hoo. They laughed and laughed.
And with every laugh, Twinkle glowed brighter. And brighter. And brighter! Until she was shining like a tiny moon.
Slowly, Twinkle began to float.
she said.
Up, up, up she flew, until she found her place in the sky.
Pip waved and waved. Then something wonderful happened. Right above him, one little star winked. Twice.
Pip smiled all the way home. And every night after that, before he went to sleep, Pip looked up and winked back.
The End.

summary.es: Una nube pequeñita que no sabe llover descubre su propia manera de ayudar.
summary.en: A tiny cloud who can't make rain discovers his very own way to help.

chapters.title: Too Small to Rain
paragraphs: High above the hills, where the birds fly and the wind sings, lived a little cloud named Nimbus.
Nimbus was soft and round, like a puff of cotton candy. But Nimbus had a problem. All the big clouds could make rain. Nimbus could not make even one drop.
Every morning, the big clouds gathered together. They grew dark and heavy, and then, splish, splash, they watered the fields below.
asked Nimbus.
Mama Cumulus, the biggest cloud of all, smiled kindly.
Nimbus squeezed and squeezed. He puffed up his cheeks. He held his breath. But nothing happened. Not a single drop.
The other clouds giggled, and Nimbus felt his edges go wobbly.
he said sadly.

paragraphs.Mama: “Being small is not the same as being no good,”

paragraphs: said Mama Cumulus.

paragraphs.Mama: “Everyone has their own way to help. You just haven't found yours yet.”

paragraphs: Nimbus wasn't so sure. That afternoon, he floated away from the others, all by himself, wondering what a little cloud could ever do.

chapters.title: The Thirsty Garden
paragraphs: Nimbus drifted over hills and valleys until he saw a tiny garden next to a little yellow house.
The garden looked very sad. The flowers were droopy. The leaves were dry and crunchy. And in the middle stood one small daisy, bending her head toward the ground.
called Nimbus.
The daisy looked up.
she sighed.

paragraphs.Daisy: “The big clouds never come this way. Our garden is too small for them to notice.”

paragraphs: Nimbus looked at the daisy. Then he looked at himself. Too small to notice. He knew exactly how that felt.
said Nimbus.

paragraphs.Daisy: “Could you just stay for a while?”

paragraphs: asked the daisy.
So Nimbus stayed. He floated right over the garden, and something surprising happened. His soft, round body made a cool, gentle shadow. The flowers stopped wilting. The daisy lifted her head.
she said.
Nimbus felt a warm, fizzy feeling inside. It was the happiest he had ever felt.

chapters.title: Nimbus Shines
paragraphs: Nimbus stayed with the garden all afternoon. He told the daisy stories about the sky, and the daisy told him about bees and butterflies.
Nimbus was so happy that he started to feel full. Full of joy, full of friendship, full of something tingly.
Then, plip! A single raindrop fell from Nimbus and landed right on the daisy's petal.
gasped Nimbus.
Plip, plop, plip! More drops fell, soft and gentle, just the right size for a small garden. The flowers drank and drank. The leaves turned green again.
cheered the daisy.

When the rain stopped, the sun peeked out from behind Nimbus. Its light shone through the last tiny drops, and a rainbow appeared over the garden. It was a small rainbow, but it was the most beautiful one Nimbus had ever seen.
That evening, Nimbus floated home to Mama Cumulus.
he said proudly.

paragraphs.Nimbus: “Small clouds can make small rain for small gardens.”

paragraphs: Mama Cumulus wrapped him in a big, fluffy hug.
she said.
And from that day on, whenever a little garden felt thirsty, Nimbus was always the first to come.
The End.

summary.es: Un conejito quiere el jardín más grande del valle y aprende que lo bueno toma tiempo y es mejor compartido.
summary.en: A bunny wants the biggest garden in the valley and learns that good things take time and are better shared.

chapters.title: The Tiny Seeds
paragraphs: Benny was a bunny with long floppy ears and a very big dream. He wanted to grow the biggest, most wonderful garden in the whole valley.
One sunny morning, Grandma Bunny gave him a little paper bag. Inside were seeds of every shape. Round seeds, flat seeds, stripy seeds, and seeds as small as freckles.
shouted Benny.
He dug little holes with his paws. He dropped in the seeds, one by one. He covered them with soft, dark soil, and he watered them with his tiny blue watering can.
Then Benny sat down and waited. And waited. And waited.
His friend Tilly the turtle came walking by, very slowly.

paragraphs.Benny: “I'm waiting for my garden to grow,”

paragraphs: said Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “It should be ready any minute now.”

paragraphs: Tilly smiled a slow, wise smile.

paragraphs.Tilly: “Gardens don't grow in minutes, Benny. They grow in days and weeks. Good things take time.”

paragraphs: Benny's ears drooped. Days? Weeks? That sounded like forever.

chapters.title: Waiting Is Hard
paragraphs: The next morning, Benny ran outside. Nothing. Just brown dirt.
The morning after that, he ran outside again. Still nothing.
said Benny. So he sang them a wake-up song.
Milo the mouse peeked out from under a leaf.
said Benny.
Milo thought for a moment.

paragraphs.Milo: “When I'm waiting for something, I keep busy. Why don't you take care of your garden while it grows?”

paragraphs: So Benny tried. Every day, he gave the soil a drink of water. He pulled out the weeds. He shooed away the hungry crows. And while he worked, he forgot to be grumpy.
Then, one morning, Benny saw something tiny and green poking out of the ground. Then another. And another!
shouted Benny, hopping in circles.
Tilly the turtle nodded.

paragraphs.Tilly: “You see? Waiting is hard. But when your paws are busy, it gets a little easier.”

chapters.title: A Garden for Everyone
paragraphs: Weeks went by, and Benny's garden grew and grew. There were tall sunflowers, plump red tomatoes, crunchy carrots, and strawberries as sweet as candy.
It was the biggest, most wonderful garden in the whole valley.
Benny was so proud. But when he looked at all that food, he had a funny feeling.

paragraphs.Benny: “This is too much for just one bunny,”

paragraphs: he said.
Then he remembered. Grandma had given him the seeds. Tilly had given him good advice. Milo had helped him keep busy. And the bees had visited every flower.
said Benny.

paragraphs.Benny: “I will share my garden with everyone!”

paragraphs: So Benny made invitations for all his friends. On Saturday, they came. Tilly brought a picnic blanket. Milo brought acorn cups. Even the crows came, and this time, Benny didn't shoo them away.
They ate carrot cake and strawberry pie. They told jokes and played games until the stars came out.
said Milo, with a very full tummy,
Benny smiled. He looked at his friends, laughing together under the sunflowers. He knew Milo was right. Not because it was the biggest garden, but because it was a garden for everyone.
The End.
